name: Antares Nuclear
summary: Antares is developing factory-produced fission microreactors for critical missions, including U.S. military applications. It announced a $470 million Series C in July 2026, with no valuation disclosed.
overview: Antares develops small fission microreactors intended for strategic and remote power applications. The company is pursuing a factory-production approach and has disclosed work with the Department of Energy and U.S. military stakeholders.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: The round included $370M in equity and $100M in debt; no company valuation was disclosed.

bull_case: Demand for resilient, deployable power at remote and strategic sites could create a meaningful market for microreactors. Antares' criticality milestone and large financing provide tangible validation for a company in an otherwise long-cycle category.
bear_case: Nuclear deployment depends on licensing, fuel supply, manufacturing and customer acceptance, each of which can delay revenue materially. The Series C size does not establish a valuation or guarantee a commercial fleet order.
directory_notes: $470M Series C announced in July 2026; valuation undisclosed.

intelligence.description: A nuclear-energy company developing factory-produced fission microreactors for critical missions.

metrics.label: Latest valuation
metrics.note: Valuation was not announced with the July 2026 Series C

company: Antares is developing fission microreactors designed for critical and remote missions, including potential U.S. military use. Its strategy is based on producing reactors in factories rather than treating every project as a bespoke construction programme.

The company announced a $470 million Series C in July 2026, comprising $370 million of equity and $100 million of debt, without disclosing a valuation. It later announced a strategic-breakthrough award for a space-reactor demonstration and a long-term TRISO fuel-supply agreement.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Antares is one of the clearest private bets on compact nuclear power for defence and other mission-critical use cases. The investment case depends on moving from engineering and demonstrations to a licensable, fuelled and repeatably manufactured product.

changed.text: Announced $470M Series C to deploy nuclear microreactors for critical missions.

takeaways: The Series C is confirmed, but the company did not disclose a valuation.
Criticality, fuel supply and licence progress are more consequential than a private valuation at this stage.
Military and remote-power demand provide a strategic wedge, but deployment remains long-cycle.
